title: Sorting
summary: Put things in order: numbers, text, and objects by one or more fields.

sections.heading: Sorting numbers
body: JavaScript's `sort()` with no argument compares items as text, so `10` comes before `9`. For numbers, pass a compare function: `(a, b) => a - b`.
Python sorts numbers correctly out of the box. `sorted(x)` gives a new list; `x.sort()` changes `x` and returns `None`.

javascript.code:
const nums = [10, 9, 1, 100]
console.log([...nums].sort())
console.log([...nums].sort((a, b) => a - b))

sections.heading: Sorting by a field
body: A JavaScript compare function returns a negative number if `a` goes first, positive if `b` goes first, and 0 for a tie.
Python asks a simpler question with `key`: "what should I sort this item by?"

javascript.code:
const people = [
  { name: 'Bo', age: 30 },
  { name: 'Al', age: 25 },
]
people.sort((a, b) => a.age - b.age)
console.log(people.map((p) => p.name))

typescript.code:
const people: { name: string; age: number }[] = [
  { name: 'Bo', age: 30 },
  { name: 'Al', age: 25 },
]
people.sort((a, b) => a.age - b.age)
console.log(people.map((p) => p.name))

python.code:
people = [{'name': 'Bo', 'age': 30}, {'name': 'Al', 'age': 25}]
people.sort(key=lambda p: p['age'])
print([p['name'] for p in people])

sections.heading: Breaking ties
body: To sort by length and then alphabetically: in JavaScript, if the first comparison is 0 use `||` to fall through to the second. In Python, return a tuple from `key`; tuples compare item by item.

javascript.code:
const words = ['pear', 'fig', 'kiwi', 'apple']
words.sort((a, b) => a.length - b.length || a.localeCompare(b))
console.log(words)

mistakes: Sorting numbers in JavaScript without a compare function.
Returning `true`/`false` from a JavaScript compare function. It must return a number.
Forgetting that JavaScript `sort` changes the original array. Copy it first with `[...items]` if needed.
